'''Nyamal''' is an [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] spoken by the [[Nyamal]] people in the [[Pilbara region of Western Australia|Pilbara region]] of [[Western Australia]].

==Kinship terms==
Nyamal has a typologically rare system of kinship terms. The kinship terms in Nyamal identify the sex of the relative, the generation they belong to (relative to the speaker), as well as their [[Moiety (kinship)|moiety]], but not the more specific relationship. For example, the father and the father's brother are identified with the same kinship term, ''mama''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Burling |first1=Robbins |title=Man's many voices: Language in its cultural context |date=1970 |publisher=Holt, Rinehart and Winston Inc. |isbn=0-03-081001-9 |pages=21–26}}</ref>
